plans.note: Review sec-21 for cap amount, mutuality, exclusion of consequential damages and whether the "Excluded Claims" definition in sec-1 carries the standard carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality/data breach, willful misconduct, fees due). Check for any sub-cap on data-breach liability.

sec-20 is the indemnification clause; confirm Vendor covers third-party IP infringement plus its own negligence/willful misconduct and data breach, that defence/control mechanics are workable, and that any Customer-given indemnity is narrow. Cross-check interaction with the cap and Excluded Claims (sec-21, sec-1).

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan Customer Responsibilities (sec-12), licence restrictions (sec-13) and General (sec-30) for any build/buy or competing-product prohibition before concluding absent.

Check the scope/structure language (sec-2), Order Form and affiliate order mechanics (sec-4) and Customer Responsibilities (sec-12) for sole-source or exclusive-provider wording; likely absent otherwise.
Look in Fees/invoicing (sec-7) and Order Forms (sec-4) for best-pricing or most-favoured-customer language; only flag if the obligation runs against us (an MFN in our favour is welcome).

Non-solicits are often buried in General (sec-30) or alongside personnel/confidentiality provisions (sec-12, sec-16); if present, test duration, scope (only personnel engaged on the Services) and the general-advertising carve-out.

sec-9 should contain termination rights; confirm we have convenience termination on reasonable notice without early-termination fees, and that Vendor lacks a symmetric mid-term convenience right. Check sec-10 for penalties triggered on our exit.

sec-8 covers term and renewal: test auto-renewal length, the non-renewal notice window measured against our tolerance, and any renewal price uplift (uplift cap is a rationale note, not a standalone flag). Pricing escalators may also sit in sec-7.

sec-28 should state governing law and forum; verify it is NY/DE/CA/England & Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than offshore arbitration. Note escalation/mediation steps and any fee-shifting.

sec-24 addresses assignment and change of control; confirm we may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger without consent, and that our change of control does not give Vendor a termination or repricing right.

sec-14 governs Deliverables and Vendor Technology ownership; sec-15 governs Customer Data. Confirm we own Deliverables we pay for and all Customer Data, with no assignment or licence-back of our IP/data beyond what is needed to deliver the Services (check any analytics/aggregated-data or feedback licence).

sec-13 is the access/licence grant; test that it extends to our Affiliates and contractors (see affiliate orders in sec-4), is not revocable or suspendable at will, and that restrictions in sec-13/sec-14 do not undercut agreed use.

sec-22 is audit rights against us; check frequency, advance written notice, business-hours/remote-first conduct, Vendor bearing its own costs, and any true-up or shortfall-payment mechanic. sec-23 (records/assurance) may impose parallel obligations.

Look for late-payment interest, early-termination or shortfall charges payable by us (sec-7, sec-10) and confirm any service-level regime in sec-3 gives us credits rather than imposing damages on us; credits in our favour are not flagged.

sec-19 holds the warranties; assess duration, whether the standard is professional/conforming performance, the remedy (re-perform, then refund) and any disclaimer that hollows it out. Acceptance testing (sec-6) and performance standards (sec-3) are related.

sec-18 should set Vendor coverage; confirm commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O and cyber limits, certificate rights and notice of cancellation, given Vendor handles Customer Data (sec-17).

Check Fees (sec-7) and Order Form mechanics (sec-4, sec-2) for minimum volumes, take-or-pay or non-reducible commitments and whether termination rights in sec-8/sec-9 provide an exit; may be handled solely at the Order Form level.

sec-11 covers transition assistance and data return; confirm a defined assistance period at agreed rates, export of Customer Data in a usable format, deletion/certification, and that it survives termination for any reason (see sec-10 effects and sec-15 data provisions).
